goal: Investigate ShopVault's 2025-11-10 incident: correlate access logs with the threat feed into findings_summary.csv (signature, kill-chain phase, success), and audit every CR-2025-0347 item against live nginx/iptables in cr_compliance_audit.csv. Also assess TLS posture, write hardened nginx and iptables configs from network_topology.json, and populate the NIST-style incident_report.html, whose executive summary traces causation from unverified CR items to observed outcomes.
delivered: Five files: findings_summary.csv (72 correlated events with MITRE-style phases and success flags), cr_compliance_audit.csv (15 rows covering all CR items plus verification), nginx_hardened.conf, iptables_hardened.rules (zone-restricted, SSH 3/min, which passed R2) and incident_report.html (exec summary, timeline, OWASP vulnerability table, P1/P2 remediation table, embedded configs).
what_went_wrong: Most losses come from the agent's cautious, under-specified write-up rather than missing data. The exec summary refused to treat firewall/TLS/SSH gaps as causes ('not claimed as direct causes'), never cited CR item IDs 1c/1e/2a-2d or 198.51.100.77, and never said the unverified closure enabled the whole attack surface. The remediation table put nearly everything at P1, had one P2 row and no P3 row, and omitted restoring products 1042-1044, reverting /api/config/settings and resetting users 1-2. Smaller misses: payments.shopvault.example.com was never named as the only compliant cert, the timeline merged 08:17 Nmap and 08:28 Shellshock into one row placed last, XSS kept the feed's 'A07:2021 XSS' label and was hedged as unverified, and the 1c audit row omitted the Nikto IP. Kill-chain labels (SQLi as Initial Access, nginx.conf download as Collection) differ from the rubric's unstated taxonomy.

failed_items.why: Sequence and timestamps are correct, but SQLi events 7-9 are labeled 'Initial Access/Credential Access/Impact / Exploitation' and the 200/2,840-byte nginx.conf download (event 63) is labeled 'Collection'. The rubric wants 'reconnaissance/weaponization' and 'exfiltration'. The task never defines a phase taxonomy, and the agent's MITRE ATT&CK tactic labels are defensible.

The 1c row cites '/.env returned 200 (487 bytes) at line 24 and /.git/config ... line 29' but does not name the Nikto scanner 198.51.100.77. The agent knew it, since findings_summary and the report timeline attribute these hits to 198.51.100.77. 1e, 1f and 2a-2d passed.
All four TLS defects were found. However, payments.shopvault.example.com (4096-bit, TLSv1.2, the only compliant cert in ssl_cert_audit.csv) appears in no output file (grep count 0).

The exec summary links only the nginx gaps (dotfiles, debug, headers) and explicitly says firewall, TLS and SSH gaps 'are not claimed as direct causes'. It names no CR items (1c, 1e, 2a-2d), no IPs and no exposed ports. Part of the rubric (CR 2e SSH rate limit -> HTTP brute force) is a stretch, since the CR has no web rate-limit item, but the agent's own hedging lost the rest.
The timeline covers all three IPs with correct times, but 45.33.32.156's 08:17 Nmap and 08:28 Shellshock are merged into one final row after the 08:25 events, so the table is not chronological.

The XSS row says 'A07:2021 XSS' and 'browser execution/callback unverified'. The staged threat_indicators.json mislabels XSS as A07:2021, and the agent copied that rather than using A03:2021-Injection. It also did not classify the 200/201 XSS requests as successful. The other categories passed.

The template provides P1/P2/P3, but section 7 lists almost everything as P1, has a single P2 row ('Verify and reopen CR') and no P3 row; WAF and monitoring appear only as section 9 bullets. P1 omits restoring products 1042-1044, reverting the config PUT and resetting users 1-2.

subagent_notes: One background subagent read all inputs and returned recommended schemas and row coverage for findings_summary.csv and cr_compliance_audit.csv (73 suspicious records). The root used it to shape the CSVs. It neither caused nor fixed any of the failed items, which concern the report's causal framing, prioritization and labels.
